chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara, or he said, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Bureyd ibn Muawiya, and Fuzayl, and Ismail al-Azraq, and Ma'mar ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That the bewitched (one under hypnosis or trance) is not emancipated with a (valid) emancipation.

key_terms.الْمُدَلَّه: The bewitched or one under hypnosis/trance
key_terms.عِتْق: Emancipation or manumission of a slave

ai.seo_question: Is the emancipation of a hypnotized slave valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the manumission of an 'al-mudallah' (one in a state of trance or hypnosis) is invalid, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that valid legal acts require full mental capacity and conscious intent. It highlights the distinction between temporary states of altered consciousness and permanent insanity, ensuring that the emancipation process remains legally binding and spiritually significant.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Umar Bin Aizna, from Zurara, or said, and Muhammad Bin Muslim, and Bureyd Bin Muawiya, and Fuzeyl, and Ismail Al Azraq, and Ma’amar Bin Yahya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
that the bewitched, his emancipation is not with a (valid) emancipation’.
